causal_reasoning: The coordinator never waits on results: 32 result_recv spans total 0.000359s of a 25.575s run (dispatch adds 0.000465s).

The coordinator is idle 76.4% of the span (union busy 6.044s, nested phases counted once); its per-row commit region is bounded (row commit max 0.2229s, dominated by commit_publish fsync/rename max 0.2062s — the ORIGINAL publication law, unchanged and not to be weakened).

Arrival rate keeps up: ~32 results over the active window (~0.7s mean inter-arrival) vs per-row commit max 0.2229s — no monotone queue growth is possible at this scale; the run tail after the last arrival is only 0.836s (pool_close/rehydrate/composite_finalize).

The single >1s drain-adjacent cost (row 31's result_put) is producer-side CPU (cpu/wall ~0.98), replicated across four independent runs (P01 t_w1/t_w2/t_w4, P03M m_w4t) and two tree versions; an independent bounded drain receiver acts on the RECEIVER side and cannot reduce producer-side serialization.

P01 H2_commit_backpressure was already refuted_at_this_scale on the P01 tree; the fresh P03M-tree profile reproduces the same shape (recv ~0.0004s, commit max ~0.22s, one CPU-bound last put), so the refutation holds on the accepted candidate tree, not just the baseline.
completion_law: Causally justified safe candidate or explicit not_admitted; no unbounded queues or weakened fsync — the explicit not_admitted branch is taken.
dependency_note: P04I depends_on P03R; this admission profiles the P03M tree (commit e36178e9d08608ace4b06e4eee199f5295cedc62 bytes) and must be committed only after the P03R verdict lands. P04R reviews the documented non-admission.

measured_receiver_facts.nested_commit_law: commit(row_id=None) outer spans wrap the per-row commit(row_id=i) child 1:1; raw sums double-count — union busy is the coordinator's true occupancy

producer_side_put_facts.attribution_bound: The recorder measures process-wide CPU ns, so the 1.8-1.9s CPU-bound last-row put is NOT further attributed (pickle probe vs gc inside it vs feeder-thread marshal beside a blocked main thread are indistinguishable here); row artifact bytes are uniform (~3.97 MB x 32 rows), so the isolated cost does not track row output size. This is a producer-side serialization cost that precedes the queue boundary.

what_would_change_the_decision: coordinator result_recv walls growing with row count (recv blocking on a saturated consumer)
per-row commit max exceeding mean inter-arrival time (monotone outbox growth, potential unbounded queue)
a producer-side put that BLOCKS on the receiver (cpu/wall far below 1) while other workers starve
commit_publish tail extending past pool_close (publication becoming the run tail)
